title: NTP-drift-triggered-api-latency-incident - retro & interim runbook (draft)
content:
Summary:

A production incident on 2025-11-08 caused sustained API server p95 latency spikes across the west-1a/1b AZs that cascaded into controller and scheduler backlog. Observable effects: delayed pod starts (~30-90s extra), increased Pending pods, transient node eviction waves in one AZ, and a small but visible customer error rate spike for streaming responses.

High-level timeline (local times):
- 02:12 - monitoring alert: apiserver.p95 latency > 800ms for 3m (west-1a, west-1b). Pager triggered.
- 02:15 - on-call (Aisha) acknowledged and began triage.
- 02:18 - etcd leader rotation observed across cluster; etcd server logs showed repeated leader election attempts.
- 02:22 - controller-manager started logging requeue/backoff warnings; Deployment controller backlog grew.
- 02:30 - scheduler queue spiked (pending pods 420 -> 1.8k over 20m).
- 02:35 - several nodes in west-1b reported kubelet eviction pressure (disk.available dropping due to journal growth from many kubelet logs).
- 03:05 - mitigations applied: isolate east/west traffic, quiesce batch deploys via feature-flag, manually force leader to stable etcd node by restarting chronyd on candidate nodes.
- 03:28 - p95 latency returned to baseline and pending queue drained over ~25m.

What we saw (signals):
- apiserver metrics: p50 ~ 40ms, p95 spiked to 1.2s, p99 hits ~ 2.3s at peak.
- etcd: term churn; repeated election_timeouts; slow proposals (apply duration p95 ~ 600-1,200ms).
- nodes: CPU mostly normal, but journald growth on nodes mounting many pods; disk pressure warnings on nodes with older journal rotation configs.
- cluster time skew: NTP offset spikes on 3 control-plane instances and 4 worker nodes (measured via chrony, timedatectl showed drift up to 8s on one control-plane).
- kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler logs contained errors referencing etcd timeouts and failed lease renewals.

Immediate hypothesis (root cause):
- A combination of intermittent host time drift (chrony / systemd-timesyncd misconfiguration after an automated image rollout) caused several control-plane machines to have >2s clock offset. etcd's raft time-sensitive leader heartbeat/election logic saw these offsets as delayed responses and triggered leader churn. Leader churn increased etcd latencies which directly affected apiserver request latencies (write-heavy operations). That produced controller/scheduler backlog and downstream pod start delays.

Why this cascaded:
- Redwood's control-plane components are sensitive to clock skew because etcd/raft timeouts are tuned tightly for latency.
- The operator image rollout (infra-image-rollout-2025-11-08) changed chrony config template on some hosts; rollout was staggered and a few hosts ended up with an incorrect chrony peer list (internal ntp pool removed).
- Once leader churn began, request amplification and long tail latencies made controllers backoff -> generate retries -> increased load.

On-call mitigations performed (what we did during the incident):
- Verified time skew: timedatectl and chronyc sources showed offset on control-plane-2 & worker-45.
- Temporary mitigation: staged restart of chronyd on affected control-plane instances and workers. Commands used:
  - sudo systemctl restart chronyd
  - chronyc tracking; chronyc sources -v
  - timedatectl status
- Promoted a stable etcd node (manual restart sequence on the nodes with correct time) to break election loop (see internal note: avoid full cluster restart).
- Temporarily increased apiserver write timeouts: added --request-timeout=15s (note: this is an emergency knob; reverted after recovery).
- Paused ongoing automated CI/CD deployments and disabled batch rollouts to reduce churn.
- Cleared excessively verbose kubelet logs by rotating journal (sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M) on nodes with disk pressure.

Why the temporary fixes helped:
- Restoring accurate time on out-of-sync nodes stopped further false leader elections.
- Short-term apiserver timeout relaxation reduced some client-level errors while the cluster stabilized.

Longer-term root-cause remediation (proposed):
- Fix the image rollout template that accidentally removed internal NTP peer entries. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-config/pull/456 (in review).
- Harden chrony/systemd-timesyncd configuration: require at least 3 internal NTP peers, enforce via an admission-validated ini template and an OS-level config-managed cron check.
- Add a cluster-level periodic check (SRE playbook job) that reports nodes with time offset > 500ms. Alert to on-call if > 1 control-plane or > 3 worker nodes per AZ deviate.
- Adjust etcd/raft election timeout recommendations for our control-plane size to be slightly more tolerant of small transient skew (document tradeoffs).
- Add better runbook automation to perform safe chrony restart + health checks instead of manual sequences.
- Improve apiserver monitoring: create a derived metric apiserver_write_latency and alert on it separately from read latencies.
- Ensure journal/log rotation config across node images are consistent; add a preflight to image rollout to validate journald MaxRetention/MaxFile parameters.

Action items and owners (short):
- Aisha: finalise postmortem and ship quick chrony configuration fix (PR referenced) - due 2025-11-14.
- Daniel: implement periodic time-offset check job + Grafana dashboard - due 2025-12-01.
- Marcel: propose conservative etcd election timeout config and run chaos tests for clock skew - due 2025-12-08.
- Priya: add apiserver_write_latency alert runbook and document emergency knob usage - due 2025-11-21.

Runbook / triage checklist (interim; to be tested and automated):
1) On pager: gather cluster-wide p95/p99 apiserver latencies and etcd leader metrics.
   - kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver
   - curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep apiserver_request_latency_seconds_bucket
   - etcdctl --endpoints=<cluster> endpoint status
2) Check node times (control-plane first):
   - sudo timedatectl status
   - chronyc sources -v
   - chronyc tracking
3) If control-plane nodes show offset > 1s: restart chronyd on affected nodes (one at a time, confirm re-sync) and monitor etcd leader stability.
   - sudo systemctl restart chronyd && sleep 10 && chronyc tracking
4) If etcd leader is flapping: identify candidate node with correct time and consider controlled restart of other control-plane components to re-establish stable leader. Avoid full cluster restarts.
5) If journal growth is causing disk pressure: rotate logs on affected nodes and increase journal vacuum size in image.
   - sudo journalctl --rotate; sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M
6) If scheduler backlog grows > threshold (500+ pending pods): pause non-critical controllers (batch deploys), and consider increasing scheduler pod replicas for capacity if autoscaling is available.
7) Communicate: post initial incident summary to #inc-1789-etcd-apiserver and page infra-owners.

Open questions / unknowns we should investigate:
- Why did the image rollout change the chrony template for only a subset of hosts? (race in config management?)
- Was there any interaction with cloud-host time-sync (host-OS level) vs container runtime time namespaces?
- Can we detect these skew conditions earlier (predictive check during image rollout)?

Notes to self / aftermath observations:
- The cluster recovered without data loss; etcd applied raft consistently once time consistent.
- We observed a small customer-visible error bump; customers using streaming endpoints saw a small retry but no sustained data integrity issues.
- The incident was a good reminder that low-level infra (NTP) can produce systemic, high-amplification failures when combined with tightly-tuned distributed systems.

References / links (internal):
- Incident ticket: SRE-1789
- Slack thread: #inc-1789-etcd-apiserver (link above)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-config/pull/456
- Chrony docs and recommended configs: https://chrony.tuxfamily.org/documentation.html

Draft status: still needs timeline log snippets (etcd log excerpts), graphs (apiserver p95 + etcd apply latency), and a short customer-facing summary. Will attach logs and dashboards before final.

If you were on-call and want a 1-line play: 
- Check control-plane time offsets first; if >1s restart chronyd one node at a time and watch etcd leader/latency. Pause deployments until stable.

-- end of draft --
